subject: general
question:
In these questions, four alternatives are given for the italicized idioms. Choose the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom:-

A fly on the wheel

options.text: a person who overestimates her/his importance
a person who cautions the people
a person who is hostile to all

solution:
The correct answer is **"a person who overestimates her/his importance."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• An idiom is a phrase or expression that typically presents a figurative, non-literal meaning attached to the phrase; but some phrases become figurative idioms while retaining the literal meaning of the phrase. 
 
• **"A fly on the wheel" means someone who thinks they are more powerful than they really are.** 
 
 
• Example: That guy's a total fly on the wheel, always acting like he gets all this stuff done on his own without the help of an entire team.
 
 
 
• Overestimate means to think that something is or will be greater, more extreme, or more important than it really is.

From the above explanation, it is clear that a person who overestimates his/her importance is said to be a fly on the wheel.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 1**.
